# Build and runtime evidence matrix

72 publishes target classifications only from this machine-readable ledger. A claim is evidence for the exact recorded commit and environment, not a transferable platform certification. Configured CI, source review, cross-compilation, and an unversioned local observation do not by themselves promote a target.

## Public target classification

| Target | Current classification | Evidence required before promotion |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Linux amd64 | build and test target; runtime certification incomplete | Real X11 hardware matrix with resize, DPI, minimize/restore, user close, texture upload, device loss/recovery, and clean shutdown |
| Windows amd64 | build-only target | Real Windows hardware matrix with the same lifecycle, input, and presentation checks |
| macOS arm64/amd64 | build-only target | Real macOS hardware matrix on each claimed architecture with the same lifecycle, input, and presentation checks |
| Browser WebGPU | WebGPU-only experimental; not broadly deployable web support | Secure-context Chromium, Firefox, and Safari matrix with rendering, input, resize/DPI, visibility, device loss/recovery, and shutdown |

## Recorded evidence

No evidence record currently meets this ledger's complete metadata contract. Historical prose and a configured workflow are not certification evidence.

## Recording a claim

Add an entry to `docs/support-evidence.json` only after the stated test runs. Every entry requires a full 40-character commit SHA, operating system, GPU and driver observation (or an explicit `not observed` value for a non-GPU test), browser and version (or `not applicable`), test type, and UTC date. Regenerate this file with `make support-doc`; CI rejects a stale document with `make support-check`. A build, unit test, or fallback-adapter result cannot promote a target to runtime-certified support.

## Browser product boundary

For v0.1, browser delivery is **WebGPU-only experimental**. It requires a secure context and does not claim broad browser availability. There is no WebGL fallback. A future broadly deployable web-games product requires a separately designed, tested, and supported fallback backend rather than a compatibility patch.

## Required runtime matrix

Before changing a target classification, run and record Linux X11, Windows, macOS, Chromium, Firefox, and Safari as applicable. For each claimed target, cover resize, DPI changes, minimize/restore, user-initiated close, texture upload, device loss/recovery, and clean shutdown. Browser entries must also record HTTPS or localhost secure-context conditions. `72 doctor` remains diagnostic-only and always reports certification as `unverified`.
